definicion.title: What is strategic planning?
definicion.description: Strategic planning is the process by which a company defines its medium- and long-term direction, translates it into measurable objectives (KPIs), and aligns every area of the organization — from senior leadership down to daily operations — to execute it consistently. It's not a document that gets filed away: it's a system of decisions and priorities that gets reviewed and adjusted with real business data.

items.question: What is Strategy?
items.answer: Strategy is the process by which a company defines its medium- and long-term direction, translates that direction into measurable objectives (KPIs), and aligns every area of the organization — from senior leadership down to daily operations — to execute it consistently. It's not a document that gets filed away: it's a system of decisions and priorities that gets reviewed and adjusted with real operating data. For a CEO or CIO, the value is that strategy stops living in a presentation and starts showing up in cash flow, profitability, and the business's corporate governance.

items.question: When does a company need strategic consulting?
items.answer: A company needs strategic consulting when plans exist but aren't executed consistently across areas, when financial indicators take weeks to become available for decision-making, or when business growth depends too heavily on the constant presence of the founder or leadership team. It's also the right moment when a mid-size or large corporation needs business transformation, IT strategy, or business continuity in the face of a change in market, technology, or organizational structure, and requires an external partner to help execute — not just diagnose.
